summary: The note is a Wikipedia-style introduction to Charlemagne, also called Charles the Great, who ruled the Franks from 768, the Lombards from 774, and became emperor in 800. It presents him as a unifier of much of Europe in the early Middle Ages and the founder of the Carolingian Empire. The three paragraphs are near-duplicate versions of the same introduction, with small wording differences in the title and description.
one_line: Charlemagne (Charles the Great), Frankish king and first recognised western European emperor since Rome's fall, who founded the Carolingian Empire.
key_facts: Charlemagne, also called Charles the Great, was numbered Charles I.
Charlemagne was born 2 April 742 and died 28 January 814.
Charlemagne was King of the Franks from 768.
Charlemagne was King of the Lombards from 774.
Charlemagne became emperor in 800, described as Emperor of the Romans in one version and Holy Roman Emperor in others.
Charlemagne united much of Europe during the early Middle Ages.
Charlemagne was the first recognised emperor in western Europe since the fall of the Western Roman Empire three centuries earlier.
The expanded Frankish state founded by Charlemagne is called the Carolingian Empire.
One version says Charlemagne united much of western and central Europe rather than much of Europe.
One version says Charlemagne was the first recognized emperor to rule from western Europe since the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
The latest version states that Charlemagne was later invalidly canonized by the antipope Paschal III.
